query: The Lamp That Went Out The fever charm over the far bed has burned down to a red glow. It should have been turned an hour ago. Sister Amaranth does every round herself, and has never once missed one. Her lamp is dark. Go and find her The evening tray is still on the ward table, every bottle full. Her office door, at the back, is open a crack, and dark. It isn't your ward You tell yourself she's only late. On your way out, the patient in the far bed is still awake, watching the dark.
